description_en: Two stone memorial pillars (approx. 13th-16th century)The two pillars are located in front of a house, by a small road's side, on the western end of Michāgāũ. Michāgāũ, or Michā, is a village found 3 km west of Khalaṅgā (Jumla Bajār).The pillars consist in stone slabs with rounded (001) or ogival (002) tops. Both are oriented north-south.Pillar 001 has its main side oriented to the north. The upper section is occupied by decorative motifs including a diamond shape and two rosettes. The central section contains a low-relief carving of a stūpa. Below it one can guess the presence of an eroded inscription in Nāgarī script.Pillar 002 is oriented to the south. The top register contains a central rosette with eight petals carved in low-relief. The lower register contains at least five lines of eroded Nāgarī inscription.Stone memorial pillars were erected throughout the Karnali Basin from the 13th to the 17th centuries. They were erected to honour war heroes (Andolfatto 2019). The presence of a stūpa on pillar 001 is instrumental for dating this object in particular, as stūpa architecture is attested in the Karnali basin from the 14th to the early 16th century. This supports a dating for this pillar between the 14th and 16th century. Pillar 002 may be situated between the 13th and 16th century.
monument_assessment: Slightly damaged (minor damages such as minor cracks, plants, missing stones in plinths), Surface damages
references: REFERENCES Andolfatto, David C. 2019. Le Pays aux Cent-Vingt-Cinq-Mille Montagnes. Etude Archéologique du Bassin de la Karnali (Népal) entre le XIIe et le XVIe siècle . Paris: Sorbonne Université.
